blocks.text:
I'm computing the N-CA-CB-CG dihedral for TRP71 by first finding the bond vectors between consecutive atoms, then starting the cross product of the first two vectors to get the normal for that plane.

Continuing the cross product to get the second normal, then dotting the two normals to get the cosine of the angle between the planes, giving roughly 59.8° before determining the sign of the dihedral.

Finishing the cross product gives k=3.840042. Taking the dot with b2 yields a positive value of about 5.995, and dividing by |b2|=1.5401 gives a positive sine term of 3.893, so chi comes out positive around +59.8° — this corresponds to the g+ rotamer.
